claims.claim: Prescription hearing aids in the U.S. range from about $1,000 to more than $6,000, with an average cost near $2,500.
claims.episode_span: A modern prescription hearing aid pair often leaves the clinic at two to four thousand dollars.

claims.supporting_quote: In the U.S., they can range from about $1,000 to more than $6,000 , but the average cost is close to $2,500

claims.claim: Hearing aids have traditionally been sold as a bundle that includes the device, hearing tests, fitting, and follow-up adjustments.
claims.episode_span: programmed the devices, and sold the hardware as part of a single bundled fee.

claims.supporting_quote: Companies often sell hearing aids as part of a bundle that can include: the hearing aid any necessary hearing tests hearing aid fitting further adjustments

claims.claim: The FDA's over-the-counter hearing aid category, for adults with perceived mild-to-moderate hearing loss, went into effect on October 17, 2022.
claims.episode_span: When over-the-counter devices became legal in the United States in 2022, the contrast became visible
claims.source_title: OTC Hearing Aids: What You Should Know | FDA
claims.supporting_quote: FDA established a new category of over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids for adults 18 years of age and older with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss that went into effect on October 17, 2022.

claims.claim: Hearing aids are FDA-regulated medical devices.
claims.episode_span: State licensure rules and FDA classification as medical devices further limited who could sell or adjust the devices, keeping distribution narrow.
claims.source_title: OTC Hearing Aids: What You Should Know | FDA
claims.supporting_quote: The FDA regulates all hearing aids to ensure safety and effectiveness for consumers.

claims.claim: OTC hearing aids can be bought in a store or online without the supervision, involvement, or prescription of a licensed health care professional.
claims.episode_span: self-fitting earbuds sold for a few hundred dollars while prescription devices continued to carry the legacy pricing structure.
claims.source_title: OTC Hearing Aids: What You Should Know | FDA
claims.supporting_quote: without the supervision, involvement, or prescription of a licensed health care professional. You can buy OTC hearing aids that meet the FDA’s requirements in a store or online.

claims.claim: Adoption of OTC hearing aids has been much lower than anticipated - only about 2% of adults with hearing difficulties have opted for them.
claims.episode_span: Adoption of the new OTC category has been slower than some expected, partly because many users still want professional verification for fit
claims.source_title: The Hearing Aid Revolution That Wasn't - Pacific Hearing Inc.
claims.supporting_quote: only about 2% of adults with hearing difficulties have opted for OTC hearing aids, indicating a much lower adoption rate than anticipated

claims.claim: A hearing aid has three basic parts — a microphone, an amplifier, and a speaker — with the microphone converting sound to electrical signals for the amplifier.
claims.episode_span: Inside each device sit a microphone, a digital signal processor, a miniature receiver, and a battery
claims.source_title: Hearing Aids | NIDCD (National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders)
claims.supporting_quote: A hearing aid has three basic parts: a microphone, amplifier, and speaker. The hearing aid receives sound through a microphone, which converts the sound waves to electrical signals and sends them to an amplifier.

claims.claim: FDA expected its 2022 OTC final rule to lower hearing-aid costs by unbundling the device purchase from professional advice, fitting, adjustment, and maintenance.
claims.episode_span: Because the hardware and the service were sold together, the price of the electronics was never isolated and therefore never directly pressured.
claims.source_title: Medical Devices; Ear, Nose, and Throat Devices; Establishing Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids (Final Rule, 87 FR 50698) | Federal Register
claims.supporting_quote: we expect this final rule to lower costs of hearing aids by unbundling the purchase of hearing aids from professional services, including professional advice, fitting, adjustment, or maintenance to make the devices available over the counter

claims.claim: The August 16, 2022 FDA final rule lets consumers with perceived mild-to-moderate hearing impairment buy hearing aids in stores or online without a medical exam, prescription, or audiologist fitting.
claims.episode_span: When over-the-counter devices became legal in the United States in 2022, the contrast became visible
claims.source_title: FDA Finalizes Historic Rule Enabling Access to Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids for Millions of Americans (FDA press announcement, Aug 16 2022)
claims.supporting_quote: enabling consumers with perceived mild to moderate hearing impairment to purchase hearing aids directly from stores or online retailers without the need for a medical exam, prescription or a fitting adjustment by an audiologist

claims.claim: Hearing aids intended for severe hearing impairment (or for users under 18) do not qualify for the OTC category and remain prescription devices.
claims.episode_span: because the most severe losses still route through clinicians
claims.source_title: FDA Finalizes Historic Rule Enabling Access to Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids for Millions of Americans (FDA press announcement, Aug 16 2022)
claims.supporting_quote: Hearing aids that do not meet the requirements for the OTC category (for example, because they are intended for severe hearing impairment or users younger than age 18) are prescription devices.

claims.claim: Hearing aids are devices regulated under the FD&C Act; air-conduction hearing aids are generally class I or class II medical devices.
claims.episode_span: State licensure rules and FDA classification as medical devices further limited who could sell or adjust the devices
claims.source_title: Medical Devices; Ear, Nose, and Throat Devices; Establishing Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids (Final Rule, 87 FR 50698) | Federal Register
claims.supporting_quote: Hearing aids are devices intended for human use and are subject to the FD&C Act. Currently, air-conduction hearing aids are generally either class I or class II devices.
